articles.title: Maricsa Alfaro: los puntos más controvertidos del fallo que permitió su liberación y las posibilidades de revertir la sentencia
articles.summary: La empresaria fue liberada en los últimos días luego que un tribunal variara su pena de cárcel efectiva por la de prisión suspendida, pese a que atropelló al vigilante Juan Martínez en estado de ebriedad y con el brevete vencido
articles.body_text: Tan solo cuatro meses estuvo en la cárcel la empresaria Maricsa Polet Alfaro Cerna por embestir y causar la muerte al vigilante Juan Martínez Torres, el pasado 3 de mayo, en la urbanización Las Palmas de El Golf, en Trujillo. El pasado 7 de octubre, la Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones de La Libertad decidió liberarla. Luego de ser sentenciada -el 5 de junio último- a cuatro años, seis meses y 26 días de prisión, Alfaro Cerna fue recluida en el penal de mujeres El Milagro, pero su defensa presentó una apelación contra dicha condena, por lo que la audiencia se efectuó el 24 de septiembre. El recurso fue analizado por los magistrados Víctor Alberto Martín Burgos Mariños, Jorge Humberto Colmenares Cavero y Manuel Federico Loyola Florián, quienes revocaron el fallo del Tercer Juzgado Penal Unipersonal Transitorio de la Unidad de Flagrancia de La Libertad y determinaron que la denunciada solo cumpla dos años de pena suspendida, es decir, en libertad. Además, establecieron que Alfaro Cerna tiene que comparecer cada 60 días ante el juzgado de ejecución para justificar y registrar sus actividades con el debido control biométrico, no variar su domicilio real sin autorización previa del juzgado de ejecución. Además, está obligada a cumplir con el pago de la reparación civil y no debe cometer un nuevo delito doloso. No obstante, dicho tribunal sí confirmó la decisión de la primera instancia respecto a la inhabilitación definitiva a la empresaria para manejar cualquier tipo de vehículo motorizado. La sentencia de la Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones de La Libertad contiene argumentaciones que pueden generar distintas opiniones, en vista que se trata de un caso en el que hay una persona fallecida y la acusada se encontraba en estado de ebriedad, ya que registraba un gramo con ochenta y cuatro centigramos de alcohol por litro de sangre (1.84 G/L), y tenía la licencia de conducir vencida. En su resolución, el tribunal recuerda que el artículo 57° del Código Penal faculta al juez a suspender la ejecución de la pena en caso cumpla ciertos requisitos. Por ello, señala que la pena impuesta a Alfaro Cerna, de 4 cuatro, seis meses y 26 días, “satisface el requisito temporal”. “Resulta inferior al límite legal de la suspensión de la ejecución de la pena”, indicó. Además, aduce que “la acusada carece de antecedentes penales y no registra la condición de reincidente o habitual”. La sala indica que el punto central del debate es el pronóstico sobre la conducta futura de la imputada, es decir que no vuelva a cometer delito doloso. “La defensa sostiene que la acusada colaboró desde el primer momento, se entregó a la policía, cumplió las reglas de conducta, efectuó pagos a cuenta de la reparación civil (que a la fecha suman S/. 130,000.00 soles), aceptó los hechos mediante conclusión anticipada y tiene arraigo domiciliario, familiar y laboral”, indica el tribunal en su argumentación. Incluso, hace hincapié en que el homicidio culposo, delito por el cual fue condenada Maricsa Alfaro, “no es un delito doloso ni se encuentra entre los delitos excluidos de la suspensión por el artículo 57° del Código Penal”. “La gravedad de la conducta ya fue tomada en cuenta al momento de realizar su tipificación (homicidio culposo agravado por conducción en estado de embriaguez); también ha sido valorada al momento imponer la pena de inhabilitación para conducir vehículos motorizados de forma definitiva”, se indica en el fallo. Incluso, remarca que en el expediente del caso no figura evidencia de que la conductora haya intentado fugar. “La acusada no tiene denuncias por incumplimiento de reglas de conducta, entregó su pasaporte, compareció a las diligencias y fue encontrada en su domicilio cuando la autoridad la requirió”, adujo el tribunal. La Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones señaló que el delito de omisión de auxilio no fue materia de ejercicio de la acción penal. “Tampoco se ha acreditado denuncia o imputación por omisión de auxilio o fuga del lugar del accidente vinculada a los hechos”, precisa. Además, considera que Maricsa Alfaro “es una persona con actividad laboral conocida y estable (gerente de una empresa), con estudios superiores y sin antecedentes penales” y que los agravantes de manejar en estado de ebriedad y de tener la licencia vencida ya fueron tomados en cuenta en la sentencia y en la inhabilitación para manejar. “La circunstancia de haber conducido con licencia vencida desde el año 2022 y bajo los efectos del alcohol es grave, pero ya fue considerada al momento de determinar el “quantum” de la pena y la inhabilitación (precisamente, la inhabilitación definitiva para conducir cualquier tipo de vehículo motorizados neutraliza el riesgo de reiteración)”, argumentó la sala. Otro hecho saltante de este caso es que se le permitió a la acusada participar en la audiencia de apelación, ya que su defensa planteó que se le interrogue. El magistrado Víctor Burgos Mariños se opuso porque señaló que “no es materia de debate la responsabilidad penal de la procesada, por lo que no cabe interrogarla”. Sin embargo, el tribunal, tras poner a votación el tema, aprobó su participación. El abogado Roberto Arteaga Robles, quien representa a los dos hijos mayores del vigilante Juan Martínez Torres, indicó a El Comercio que, por el lado de la parte demandante, solo puede apelar en el tema de la reparación civil. En el proceso hay otros letrados que ejercen la defensa de los otros cuatro hijos de la víctima. “En el tema de la ejecución no podemos participar porque es un tema del Ministerio Público. Sí podemos argumentar y plantear la nulidad de la sentencia, pero eso queda a discreción de los hijos mayores”, afirmó. Consideró que la Segunda Sala de Apelaciones de La Libertad “ha valorado de forma segmentada” dicho caso. “Una cosa es la apelación de la ejecución, que es por parte de Maricsa Alfaro, y otra cosa es la apelación por la reparación civil. En el tema de la aceptación de la responsabilidad ya no se puede discutir porque ya se aceptó la responsabilidad, solamente se está viendo la ejecución o la suspensión”, afirmó. “No se puede apelar en otro sentido porque en primera instancia fue favorable y ella fue sentenciada. Sí puede apelar el tema de la reparación, pero el tema de la pena no se puede aumentar ni reducir”, agregó. Arteaga explicó que la reciente sentencia estableció que Alfaro Cerna pague una reparación de 400 mil soles, pero la defensa había pedido un monto de 600 mil soles debido a que en el proceso se ha acreditado que Juan Martínez Torres tuvo seis hijos en tres parejas, pero solo se ha reconocido a la esposa. Johnny Aurazo Murrugarra, editor del diario Correo de La Libertad, contó a El Comercio que la liberación de la empresaria Maricsa Alfaro ha causado indignación en la ciudadanía de Trujillo, incluso la prensa local ha tomado con sorpresa esta decisión del Poder Judicial, pues no esperaba un fallo de esta naturaleza. Explicó que los ciudadanos trujillanos cuestionan que en el caso de Adrián Villar, quien atropelló y causó la muerte de la deportista Lizeth Marzano en Lima, se le haya dictado prisión preventiva, mientras que Maricsa Alfaro fue liberada, pese a que se comprobó que manejaba en estado de ebriedad y tenía la licencia de conducir vencida desde el 2022. Incluso, Aurazo Murrugarra aseguró que, de acuerdo con sus fuentes, la noticia de la liberación de Alfaro Cerna también ha sorprendido al Ministerio Público, que esperaba una ratificación de la condena impuesta a la imputada. En cuanto a los integrantes de la Segunda Sala Penal de Apelaciones de La Libertad, Aurazo comentó que se trata de magistrados de “amplia experiencia” y recordó que dos de sus integrantes han estado a cargo de casos de bastante relevancia en el norte del país. En ese contexto, el periodista recordó que los magistrados Víctor Burgos Mariños y Jorge Colmenares Cavero, junto a Manuel Sosaya López, entonces miembros de la Primera Sala Penal de Apelaciones, condenaron en el 2019 a 30 años de cárcel al coronel PNP en situación de retiro y exalcalde de Trujillo, Elidio Espinoza, por el caso ‘Escuadrón de la Muerte’. Además, Víctor Burgos Mariños entabló una querella, en octubre de 2023, a Arturo Fernández, entonces alcalde de Trujillo, debido a que este último lo acusó públicamente de corrupción y de vincularlo con una supuesta red criminal denominada ‘Los Cuellos Blancos del Norte’. La Segunda Sala de Apelaciones de la Corte Superior de Justicia de La Libertad ratificó, en enero del 2026, la condena de un año y ocho meses de pena suspendida para Fernández.

articles.title: Huracán Simón de categoría 4 EN VIVO | nueva trayectoria, cuándo y dónde tocará tierra en México
articles.summary: El lento desplazamiento del huracán Simón frente a Jalisco amenaza con prolongar los efectos más severos en la costa de México, con vientos de hasta 230 km/h, olas de nueve metros y lluvias extraordinarias
articles.body_text: Los últimos pronósticos del domingo redujeron las posibilidades de que el huracán Simón toque tierra en México, sin que disminuyan los riesgos de fuertes lluvias y vientos severos. El ciclón avanza a un ritmo peligrosamente lento y paralelo a la costa del Pacífico en una categoría 4 de 5 en la escala Saffir Simpson. Los efectos suelen golpear más a medida que pasa más tiempo en un mismo lugar. Pero “parece estar sintiendo los efectos del terreno alto” de la cadena montañosa que atraviesa esta región, indicó la agencia de huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC) en su boletín más reciente. El NHC observó que es “cada vez más probable que Simón evite tocar tierra directamente a corto plazo”. El gobierno mexicano prevé “que se debilite paulatinamente durante las próximas horas”, según su último reporte. Un equipo de la AFP fue a Puerto Vallarta, una joya turística que será golpeada por los efectos del huracán. Las autoridades piden a los paseantes alejarse del malecón. Las olas rompían con fuerza sobre este paseo y el agua rebasaba una estatua de un caballito de mar de unos dos metros. “Ven la ola y parece que les dicen arrímense (acérquense)”, reprochó una policía sobre un grupo de turistas que se acerca a tomar fotos e ignora la indicación de alejarse de la orilla. “Vemos a varias personas que les cuesta un poco acatar indicaciones y se ponen en riesgo”, indicó la oficial Claudia Matías. Los negocios protegieron ventanas y puertas con tablones, y en algunos pintaron en aerosol mensajes como “Simón dice: ‘todo va a estar bien’”, en referencia al popular juego en el que los niños siguen instrucciones, o “Simón, sé breve, pacífico” junto al dibujo de un tiburón y caras felices. Manuel Jaime, habitante de Vallarta de 37 años, caminaba en la acera de enfrente, llena de negocios tapiados. Salió a pasear con su familia para relajarse. “En esta ocasión parece ser que va a estar muy tranquilo el puerto, esperemos que sí”, dijo. Pero la intensidad de la lluvia y la marea incrementa hacia la tarde. Vicente García, un turista de 48 años, proveniente de California, coincide. “Esperábamos una tormenta más grande ayer, así que permanecimos adentro, pero me alegra que no fuera así”, indicó. “Ya nos vamos mañana”. Por la mañana el gobierno mexicano estimó que hacia las 18H00 locales del domingo el centro del ciclón llegaría a unos 15 km de las costas del estado de Jalisco. Aunque no toque tierra “todas las bandas nubosas del ciclón o la parte intensa del ciclón de todos modos va a estar afectando” poblados a la orilla del mar, explicó a la AFP el director del servicio meteorológico de México, Fabián Vázquez. “Vamos a tener efectos muy severos sobre todo de viento en la costa” con olas de hasta nueve metros y lluvias extraordinarias, añadió. El sábado, la Marina de México evacuó por barco a un centenar de personas de poblados costeros amenazados por Simón. En Puerto Vallarta, decenas de habitantes comenzaron a llegar a los refugios provenientes de colonias en riesgo por inundaciones. “A lo mejor si llega el huracán, va a levantar la casa y por eso mejor decidimos venir a un refugio”, dice José de Jesús Santillán, albañil de 55 años, sentado en un camastro. En otro albergue permanece Raquel García, de 58 años. Vive en una zona de riesgo por inundaciones. Pero no le preocupan demasiado las pérdidas materiales. “Con el tiempo, lo vamos a recuperar (...) yo prefiero mi vida y la de mi esposo que las cosas”.

articles.title: Cusco: dos incendios forestales activos en Calca y La Convención
articles.summary: Dos incendios forestales continúan activos en las provincias de Calca y La Convención, en la región Cusco, donde las autoridades concentran sus esfuerzos en controlar las emergencias, informó Miguel Ángel Ocsso, jefe de la Oficina de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres del Gobierno Regional del Cusco.
articles.body_text: Dos incendios forestales continúan activos en las provincias de Calca y La Convención, en la región Cusco, donde las autoridades concentran sus esfuerzos en controlar las emergencias, informó Miguel Ángel Ocsso, jefe de la Oficina de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres del Gobierno Regional del Cusco. En declaraciones a TV Perú, el funcionario explicó que ambos siniestros se ven favorecidos por las condiciones climáticas, como la vegetación seca, los vientos y la intensa radiación solar, factores que dificultan las labores de control del fuego. Ocsso precisó que el incendio de Calca lleva varios días activo, mientras que el registrado en La Convención es más reciente. Para atender las emergencias, se desplegaron brigadas, bomberos, personal de las Fuerzas Armadas y otros equipos de respuesta. El jefe de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres informó que Cusco acumula cerca de 289 incendios forestales en lo que va del año. Aclaró que esta cifra corresponde al total de emergencias registradas y no al número de incendios que permanecen activos. Asimismo, indicó que alrededor de 9.000 hectáreas resultaron afectadas por el fuego durante este año. La cifra es inferior a las aproximadamente 15.000 hectáreas reportadas en el mismo periodo de 2025 y a las más de 30.000 hectáreas registradas en 2022. El funcionario destacó el trabajo coordinado entre las instituciones para combatir estos siniestros, aunque advirtió que la atención puede complicarse cuando se producen varias emergencias al mismo tiempo o no se cuenta con suficiente personal. Como ejemplo, señaló que la semana pasada se registraron cerca de 14 incendios forestales en la región, los cuales fueron extinguidos. Ocsso también lamentó que los incendios forestales hayan causado cinco muertes en Cusco en lo que va del año. Entre las víctimas se encuentran tres adultos mayores y dos hermanos, una niña de 11 años y un adolescente de 18 años. Ante esta situación, el Gobierno Regional coordina acciones con el programa Pensión 65 y la Gerencia Regional de Desarrollo e Inclusión Social para reforzar la prevención, especialmente entre los adultos mayores, y evitar que más personas pierdan la vida al intentar controlar las quemas.

articles.title: Ambani's Jio seeks to raise $3.2B in what could be India's biggest IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Jio plans to use most of its IPO proceeds to repay debt as it expands beyond telecom.
articles.body_text: Jio Platforms, the digital arm of Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries, is seeking to raise as much as $3.2 billion in what could be India’s biggest initial public offering. The listing will test public-market appetite for a company that attracted more than $20 billion from global investors, including Google and Meta in 2020. On Wednesday, Reliance Industries said in a stock exchange filing (PDF) that Jio had set a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 (about $11.19 to $11.76) per share for the offering of up to 270 million new shares (PDF). The IPO will open for subscription on October 21 and close on October 23, with bidding for anchor investors scheduled for October 19. At the upper end of the proposed price band, the IPO would value Jio at about ₹10.3 trillion (around $108.3 billion), based on the number of shares expected to be outstanding after the offering. In 2020, Jio was valued at up to ₹4.91 trillion ( about $65 billion at the time). Meta, then known as Facebook, invested $5.7 billion , while Google committed $4.5 billion . Jio’s IPO is set to overtake Hyundai Motor India’s ₹278.7 billion ($3.3 billion at the time) offering in 2024, the country’s biggest to date, even if its shares are priced at the lower end of the range. Jio’s IPO comes as Elon Musk has stepped up his criticism of Ambani , accusing him of trying to keep Starlink out of India. The accusation comes more than a year after Jio and rival Airtel signed deals with Musk’s SpaceX to distribute Starlink’s satellite internet service in India, subject to regulatory approvals. Indian authorities have rejected Musk’s claims . In the quarter ended June, Jio’s revenue rose nearly 12% from a year earlier to ₹391.7 billion (about $4.1 billion), while its net profit climbed 9% to ₹77.6 billion (around $816 million), per its IPO prospectus (PDF). Jio has set aside shares worth up to ₹25 billion (about $263 million) for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders and another ₹5 billion ($53 million) for employees, who will receive a discount of ₹54 per share. Of the IPO proceeds, Jio plans to use up to ₹275 billion ($2.9 billion) to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, with the remaining proceeds going toward general corporate purposes, per the prospectus. articles.title: Flock CEO says its microphones detect 'just gunshots' — its website says different | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Langley’s comments come amid mounting scrutiny of Flock from privacy advocates, including the ACLU, and members of the public who are concerned about the misuse of its technology.
articles.body_text: Flock CEO Garrett Langley said the company’s gunshot-detection microphones detect “just gunshots,” but Flock’s website paints a far broader picture of what other ambient audio also gets picked up. Speaking onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , the co-founder of the surveillance company defended Flock’s audio-collection product called Gunshot Detection , which listens for gunshots and other ambient audio across nearby neighborhoods to provide “earlier awareness” to potential public safety events. Flock’s website says that the company’s audio systems can pinpoint gunfire instantly, while also being able to “detect street takeovers early to stop chaos before it escalates,” and “identify severe crashes in real time so help arrives faster.” It also says they can “expand awareness beyond gunfire with alerts for car crashes, fireworks, and sideshows.” During the interview, Langley pushed back against what he described as misinformation about his product, arguing that many of its critics misunderstand how its products work. The comments come as public opinion continues to shift against Flock and other license plate reading companies amid growing unease about mass surveillance — sentiments that were visible in San Francisco, where protesters gathered to voice their opposition outside the venue as Langley took the stage. “Most people don’t call 911 when they hear a gunshot, and so that’s why we built the product,” Langley told TechCrunch editor-in-chief Connie Loizos onstage. “And then some of our customers said, ‘Oh, we have these in parking lots. It would be great if we could get alerted if someone was being abducted, if someone was being harmed.’” Langley said that the idea seemed logical, so the company prototyped it and rolled it out to a couple of customers, but said that some people then had a lot of concerns. Langley conceded to making mistakes but that he was listening to his customers. “There’s only a couple customers that were prototyping it with us, and we said, ‘OK, great, it’s just going to do gunshots, plain and simple.’ If a gun goes off, we’ll notify, and if not, that’s all it’s going to listen to,” said Langley. When asked about the contradiction between his remarks and the company’s marketing materials that say the audio systems can detect more than gunshots, he responded, “It’s just gunshots.” When reached by TechCrunch, Flock spokesperson Paris Lewbel said: “Flock’s gunshot detection technology is primarily used to detect gunfire but is also capable of detecting fireworks, sideshows, and potential car crashes. CEO Garrett Langley’s remarks were intended to emphasize that Flock’s Audio Detection technology is not designed to monitor conversations or analyze speech and does not currently detect human screaming or distress.” An FAQ section of the website notes that “in addition to gunshots, Flock Gunshot and Audio Detection can detect fireworks, sideshows, and other disruptive community events.” It goes on to state that the company’s “detection library is continually expanding to include emerging threats that are relevant” to customers’ specific needs. Langley stated that the number of Flock’s microphones is comparable to ShotSpotter, which as of 2024 had about 25,000 microphones, per reporting by Wired . articles.title: Colossal Biosciences announces new AI platform to help accelerate de-extinction efforts | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Colossal announced a new AI platform to help accelerate its de-extinction efforts and Peter Diamandis has launched a new fund to back startups who use it.
articles.body_text: Colossal Biosciences announced Wednesday a new AI platform to help accelerate its efforts to bring back extinct species, TechCrunch can exclusively report. The platform, called GenoMorph, uses advanced 3D morphology, comparative genomics, and developmental biology to identify genes that could be edited in de-extinction projects with limited gene data. The company is using it as part of its effort to bring back the dodo bird, for which there are limited genomes to work with. For example, the company is working with only one dodo genome compared to the 100 genomes it has been able to obtain as part of its woolly mammoth de-extinction project. DNA from the woolly mammoth is more plentiful because the colder climates the animal lived in preserve the DNA better than the tropics where the dodo lived, the company said. “Normally, scientists can compare many genomes to understand which genetic differences are responsible for certain traits,” Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm told TechCrunch. “We don’t have that luxury with ancient DNA from extinct species whose DNA is severely limited, and we can only get a small number of complete genomes.” To build GenoMorph, Lamm said the company collected a bunch of developmental data from “chickens, quail, ducks, and pigeons,” and combined it with the “genetic information and 3D skull measurements from more than 70 bird species.” He said it took more than a year of work to build this platform, which also builds on the company’s years of work in de-extinction. “The AI learns which regions of DNA are active as different birds develop their beaks and facial structures, and uses that information to predict which genetic switches may have given the dodo its iconic appearance.” He said to think of the platform as a “treasure map for the dodo genome,” where, rather than searching through a bunch of potential genetic differences, GenoMorph can help the Colossal team find only the genetic differences that matter. “So far we’ve identified approximately 2,300 promising DNA editing targets for the dodo cranial facial morphology that we can now test in the lab,” he continued. He said GenoMorph will help the company tackle one of its biggest bottlenecks in trying to de-extinct animals — finding out which changes actually make an extinct species unique. But Lamm said scientists also need to test whether those edits can create the physical traits they need. “We’ve developed a new system that uses lipid nanoparticles to deliver gene-editing tools directly into developing bird embryos,” he said. This will help the team see how certain genetic changes impact the development of a bird “without having to wait through an entire breeding cycle that requires birds to reach sexual maturity.” The company also announced Wednesday that its Nicobar pigeon colony now has 36 birds and that it has successfully created the essential cells that become eggs and sperm. “Because the Nicobar pigeon is the dodo’s closest living relative, those cells are a critical part of our strategy for creating birds that carry dodo traits,” he said. Next, the company is hoping to prove what GenoMorph predicts in a lab. “What’s most exciting is that we’re reaching a point where the different technologies we’ve been developing are starting to converge together and help other projects we are working on in a completely different part of the tree of life,” Lamm continued. When asked whether it was safe to edit genes this way, Lamm said the point of developing a technology like GenoMorph is to make genetic engineering “more precise, controlled, and testable.” He said the product doesn’t edit genes itself, but helps their team identify which genetic changes are worth investigating. “Identifying a potential edit doesn’t mean we immediately introduce it into an animal or assume it’s safe,” he continued. “The more precisely we can identify and validate these changes, the more informed our decisions become throughout the process.”

articles.title: Flock CEO: We haven't 'fired' any police departments as customers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Flock CEO Garrett Langley said that the surveillance company has not canceled contracts of any police department or law enforcement agency, despite reports of abuse.
articles.body_text: Flock CEO Garrett Langley said that his company has not ended any contracts with its customers over abuse of its products. Speaking to TechCrunch editor-in-chief Connie Loizos at the Disrupt 2026 conference in San Francisco, Langley responded to criticisms facing the company about the misuse of its license plate reader cameras by police departments. It comes after streams of reporting identifying dozens of police officers who have been arrested, fired, or told to resign after being caught abusing access to Flock’s nationwide database of license plate detections, oftentimes to stalk people without permission. Langley told Loizos that the company would end a relationship with a customer where there was clear widespread abuse of its systems. But, the CEO said, it has not to date “fired” a customer, as he put it, such as a police department or law enforcement agency. Langley said Flock had the debate internally, but argued that the company should not take away its product from a community that might need it in its efforts to fight crime. “If a customer knowingly broke the law, we would fire them immediately. That’s very easy,” Langley said. “Most of the debate is nuanced into ‘what if two officers out of fifty were caught?’ Today, we haven’t fired any customers, but it’s not off the table in the case of some pretty drastic law-abiding issue,” added Langley. The abuse of Flock’s systems and the data it collects is the latest in an array of controversies embroiling the Atlanta, Georgia-based maker of license plate reader cameras. Flock has more than 100,000 cameras around the United States, which allow local police departments and federal agencies to track the whereabouts of vehicle license plates and people as they pass by. By allowing its law enforcement customers to track license plates outside of their jurisdictions, some police departments can track cars across the entire country through Flock’s national central database. There have been multiple reports of Flock reactivating cameras against their customers’ wishes, prompting local residents to tape trash bags over the cameras and other times destroying them . While Langley spoke on the Disrupt stage, demonstrators gathered outside the venue to protest against Flock’s AI-powered surveillance, wearing costumes like the red robes from “The Handmaid’s Tale” and cardboard replicas of Flock cameras on their heads, while clips from the “1984” movie played on a loudspeaker behind them. Others carried signs declaring “Flock off,” or “Flock = ICE.” Flock does not have a direct contract with the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), but the agency has reportedly accessed Flock data in the past by collaborating with local police departments that use Flock cameras. Ashley Ortiz, an organizer with local progressive activist group The Wolves, told TechCrunch that she wants local lawmakers to take constituents’ concerns about Flock more seriously. “I think Flock is going to be the start of a lot more community building, because we can come together around something as bipartisan as not enjoying mass surveillance,” said Ortiz. “We have Republicans who join us, conservatives who agree, we have sovereign citizens cutting down Flock cameras, so it’s not just the left who doesn’t want AI-powered mass surveillance.”

articles.title: Electric vehicle sales in the US are showing signs of life | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The electric vehicle market in the U.S. has been growing for the last three consecutive quarters.
articles.body_text: Don’t go writing the obituary for the U.S. electric vehicle just yet. After sales tanked following the cancellation of tax credits last year, they’ve been growing for the last three consecutive quarters, according to a new report from Cox Automotive . EVs captured 6.1% of the U.S. market, their best showing since the third quarter of 2025. The data shows that the EV market is “finding its footing again,” Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, said in an analysis that accompanied the new report. EV prices have become more competitive, and high gas prices have sparked renewed consumer interest, she added. Toyota, Rivian, and Subaru led the pack. Sales of the Toyota bZ and Lexus RZ about doubled following a refresh that hit dealerships late last year. The updated models adopted Tesla-style charging ports and received larger batteries, more powerful motors, and faster charging times. Meanwhile, Tesla’s sales dropped by 20% year-over-year. Tesla still retains the first-mover advantage, though, selling over half of all EVs during the third quarter. The recovery in the U.S. mimics what occurred in Germany after the government stopped incentives for EV purchases in November 2023, a year earlier than expected. The following month, sales fell by more than half. But after hitting that low, the market steadily recovered. German EV sales in August, the most recent month for which data is available, were the second highest on record. Get 50% off a second pass The Disrupt experience is meant to be shared. articles.title: TimeTeller puts our internal clocks at the center of personalized medicine | TechCrunch
articles.summary: German startup TimeTeller has developed a saliva test kit to help anyone understand their circadian rhythm; it aims to reduce side effects from cancer treatments.
articles.body_text: At-home health testing has been mired in overblown claims and outright fraud. But German startup TimeTeller , which has developed a saliva test kit to help anyone understand their circadian rhythm, is led by CEO Angela Relógio, who is the polar opposite of Theranos’ disgraced founder Elizabeth Holmes. Relógio is a physicist-engineer and molecular biologist who spent years researching oncology, circadian biology, and systems medicine in Germany before leaving academia to build TimeTeller. She is careful about what the test can and can’t do today. It would be easy to oversell: Relógio’s last name means “clock” in her native Portuguese, and TimeTeller has the potential to reduce side effects from cancer treatment and improve outcomes by timing treatment to each patient’s internal clock. That’s also why she’s careful to warn that TimeTeller itself operates on two timelines. The long-term goal is to determine when cancer treatments will be better tolerated and most effective, and doing so much more granularly than just telling whether someone is a morning person or a night owl. But its direct-to-consumer kit won’t help patients figure that out on their own. “That is something that we need to calculate for every single medicine; we do that in the context of clinical studies,” Relógio cautioned. According to Relógio, TimeTeller started accepting direct orders because of demand from longevity clinics, which focus on healthy aging and understand that individual data on a person’s circadian rhythm can be used to offer personalized advice on sleep, nutrition, light exposure, and physical activity. TimeTeller could also apply to metabolic diseases (such as diabetes) and neurodegenerative diseases (such as Alzheimer’s), performance, and women’s health, but cancer is its core mission. It was while studying cancer that Relógio made the discovery that led her to leave academia. She noticed that many cancer patients stopped or started their treatment because of side effects. “As a scientist, that was just impossible to watch, particularly when I was convinced that part of the problem might not only be what treatment we give, but when we give it,” Relógio said. This led her to develop the circadian rhythm test at the core of TimeTeller — which she knew had to become a company. “I personally funded our first patent because I strongly believed that this discovery should not remain in scientific publications,” she said. The startup spun out of Berlin’s Charité university hospital but has since moved to Medical School Hamburg, which provided access to patients and funding. It also offered a fallback: backup employment for TimeTeller’s team of 10 if the company couldn’t pay them. That’s a safety net TimeTeller may not need. Having enlisted biochemist and market access specialist Benjamin Dose as a co-founder, the startup secured a partnership with Techniker Krankenkasse, one of Germany’s largest health insurance providers. The partnership started out as a reimbursement deal in which the insurer pays back the cost of the test for a subset of cancer patients, and both sides are now ready to expand it to more of the insurer’s 12 million members, Relógio said. Despite her caveats about the direct-to-consumer test, TimeTeller has become a solution that cancer patients can actually access. Ahead of her appearance at TechCrunch Disrupt, where Relógio appeared onstage today in San Francisco as part of our storied Startup Battlefield competition, she made clear that the company has broader ambitions: a future in which asking “when” is central to precision medicine, because “almost every process in our body is timed.” You aren’t too late to join the action at Disrupt . articles.title: Ambrosia Energy will build a 10 GWh factory in Texas to make batteries for off-grid data centers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Startup Ambrosia Energy will build a massive factory to crank out batteries to augment solar panels, creating a round-the-clock clean power plant.
articles.body_text: Ambrosia Energy has begun work on a massive, 10 gigawatt-hour battery factory near Austin, Texas, co-founder and CEO Ben Longmier announced onstage Tuesday at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco. “That allows us to build about a 300 megawatt power plant per year out at our field sites,” he said. The factory will occupy 150,000 square feet, and Longmier said that Ambrosia plans to reach full production in two to three years. The startup emerged from stealth in June to build power plants for data centers at a cost of $100 per megawatt hour. Longmier and his co-founder, Sara Spangelo, had settled on solar plus batteries as the cheapest option that’s the fastest to deploy. Solar panels power the load during the day and charge the batteries, which discharge at night and on cloudy days to keep the data center operating round the clock. Longmier and Spangelo previously founded the satellite constellation startup Swarm, which they sold to SpaceX. Ambrosia is also beginning work on its first commercial power plant in West Texas later this year, Longmier said. The facility will pair 300 megawatts of solar panels with 660 megawatt-hours of batteries to deliver 30 megawatts of continuous power, with a goal of 99.3% uptime. Even with “overbuilding” solar and batteries to deliver continuous uptime, Longmier said the company can be profitable at $100 per megawatt-hour, making it competitive with natural gas turbines that many hyperscalers are planning to use to power their data centers. Sections of Ambrosia’s first pilot-scale power plant have been operating continuously for more than 100 days, Longmier said. The pilot is capable of generating 200 kilowatts of electricity 24/7. To hit its cost targets, Ambrosia has been finding ways to simplify its components, including solar mounts and battery packs. By reducing part counts, and manufacturing many components in a factory, the startup has been able to reduce costs relative to buying from outside suppliers. “We buy existing cells and we make our own pack in-house, and it has the fewest parts by a factor of about 100 compared to any other competitor we’ve seen,” Longmier said. ”We’ve been able to get to about 1.3x the cost of the bare cell compared to about a 5- or 7x for most stationary storage systems.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Hiyd is a health tracker that attaches to the watch you already wear | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Former Apple engineers figured out how to get a biometric sensor to attach to your watch without any magnets or adhesives.
articles.body_text: If you’re a watch enthusiast, you probably don’t want to exchange your prized timepiece for a bulky fitness tracker. But Hiyd founder Salah Batroukh doesn’t think people should have to sacrifice fashion for function. “We don’t think that health tracking needs to be this overly conscious decision where you have to change something about the way you look,” Batroukh told TechCrunch. “That’s the ethos of the entire company. Our plan is to build out this product ecosystem of invisible health tracking.” Hiyd’s first device to make health tracking look cooler is a small, slim disc that attaches to the back of your watch via microsuction , a material technology that allows the sensor to sit flush under your watch without magnets or adhesive. That way, it won’t leave any residue or mess with the mechanics of watches that keep time using magnets. “Microsuction is essentially a textured silicone, with hundreds of tiny pockets per square inch molded into a pliable sheet. So when you press on it, it pushes air out of all those pockets, and you end up with a vacuum — just like traditional suction cups but scaled down incredibly,” Batroukh explained. “It works incredibly at stopping shear forces, but a little bit of prying allows it to pop right off, which is ideal for us. It’s also incredibly thin at just 0.3 mm with our manufacturing processes.” According to Batroukh, the sensor, which measures 2.7 mm thick and weighs 7 grams, collects biometrics similar to those of leading wearables, including heart rate, heart rate variability, sleep staging, movement, calories burned, and VO2 max estimations, then syncs to an iOS or Android app. In order to fine-tune the sensor, Hiyd’s team is filming themselves doing various activities, then labeling those datasets to train its AI. “We go for a walk and say, ‘This is somebody walking, this is somebody jogging, this is somebody running,’” he said. “The one thing that AI is really good at is data analysis, so we can basically fit a lot of heuristic analysis into our sets really quickly.” On its app, Hiyd is also working to incorporate nutrition tracking. The goal isn’t to count calories, but rather to help users glean insights about how their eating habits impact their sleep quality or workout performance. “What we will do is say like, ‘Hey, on days where you work out at 10 p.m. instead of 10 a.m., your sleep quality is actually worse,’ and that’ll be specific to you,” he said. “Or it’ll say, ‘Hey, we think you had a less deep sleep last night because you had a slice of cake before you went to bed, and the sugar affected it.’” Batroukh spent about seven years as a manufacturing design engineer at Apple, a company synonymous with iconic hardware. But he wanted to know if he could design something great without the support of a global brand and a multitrillion-dollar market cap. “One of the reasons I left Apple was a lot of the products became a little bit more about being an Apple product, rather than being something for the customer,” he said. “[Hiyd] gives me the opportunity to do the exact opposite.” Batroukh is joined by fellow founders Omar Shakir, an experienced mechanical engineer who is the startup’s CTO, and Mahamad Charawi, who is its head of software. (Charawi previously co-led the Y Combinator-backed startup Laudspeaker through its sale .) Hiyd is bringing its tiny sensor to the big stage at TechCrunch Disrupt, where the company is competing as one of the top 20 companies at Startup Battlefield on Wednesday. ( Don’t miss out on the action .) In November, the company plans to launch a Kickstarter. So far, over 16,000 people have made deposits to secure Hiyd’s first units.

articles.title: Trump om Grönland: ”En enorm bit land”
articles.summary: USA och Danmark har kommit överens om Grönland. Trots det fortsätter Trump ta upp ”den vackra” ön.
articles.body_text: USA och Danmark har kommit överens om Grönland. Trots det fortsätter Trump ta upp ”den vackra” ön. – Det ägdes av Danmark, säger Trump på onsdagskvällen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Efter många turer fram och tillbaka och stundtals bitter stämning mellan USA och Danmark nådde parterna en överenskommelse i slutet av september. Den innebar att USA inte längre skulle hota att ta över Grönland, men tillåter dem att ha en högre militär närvaro i Arktis. Danmark hade hoppats att det skulle vara slutet på historien. Men de senaste två dagarna har president Donald Trump tagit upp Grönland på nytt. I ett inlägg på Truth Social i går lyfte han något som inte var nedskrivet i avtalet. Han skrev att USA ska inleda en ”massiv” kartläggning av olja, gas och mineraler på ”vårt nya och vackra Grönland”. Han fortsatte inlägget med att skriva om hur viktig ön är för USA och Europa ur ett säkerhetsperspektiv. Inlägget blev ett huvudbry för danska utrikesdepartementet. I en kommentar till tidningen BT skriver departementet att USA bara får undersöka Grönlands naturtillgångar inom ramen för grönländsk lag. ”Avtalet av den 22 september 2026 mellan Grönland, Danmark och USA förändrar inte detta. Avtalet ger inte amerikanska investerare någon särställning i förhållande till investerare från andra Natoländer, EU-länder och Natopartner när det gäller tillgången till naturresurser på Grönland” , skriver departementet. Trump lämnade det inte där. På torsdagskvällen, svensk tid, höll presidenten ett tal för republikanska väljare i Arizona. Då började han prata om Kanada som en ”51:a delstat” – och Grönland.

articles.body_text: Det är onsdag och den dag i veckan då eleverna på Sigtuna bär den traditionsenliga skoluniformen. Plötsligt har landets blickar riktats mot skolan och det som pågår i hemlighet. – Det känns otäckt, klart man var orolig för treorna på skolan men jag trodde inte att det skulle vara så här grovt, säger en elev som går första året. Sigtunaskolan humanistiska läroverket, SSHL, har ökat bevakningen sedan i fredags, när nyheten briserade om misstänkta sexuella övergrepp på ett av elevhemmen. Efter det pågick skytteltrafik från skolan med föräldrar och taxibilar som hämtade elever på löpande band. Många av eleverna har egen bil, så kallad A-traktor, av märket Range Rover, Audi och BMW, vilka står parkerade nedanför det omfattande skolområdet. På onsdagen har skolan ställt upp två stora svarta SUV:ar utanför entrén, märkta med ”Embassy Security”. Två elever, bägge män i 18-årsåldern, sitter häktade för grovt sexuellt ofredande, grovt olaga tvång och grov misshandel mot andra elever. En tredje elev har häktats misstänkt för två fall av misshandel och två fall av olaga tvång. – Det är boysen! articles.title: Tidigare C- och V-toppar ryker ihop i Aktuellt | Expressen
articles.summary: Den 13 september går Sverige till val. Följ Expressens direktrapport med senaste nytt inför valet.
articles.body_text: Centerpartiet och Vänsterpartiet har svårt att komma överens om regeringsbildning. Till SVT:s Aktuellt bjöds de tidigare partitopparna Maud Olofsson (C) och Ulla Andersson (V) in för att diskutera just detta – men då rök de ihop. På en fråga om V borde mjuka upp sina röda linjer i förhandlingarna säger Andersson att C stoppat två regeringsalternativ. – Era väljare har gjort en värderingsmässig förflyttning. Och jag tror att vi kan samlas i de värderingarna om människors lika värde säger hon. – Vet du Ulla, du är oförskämd när du säger det där. Att ni har en dröm som ni måste ge upp. Det kommer inte hålla om man ska samarbeta att ha den attityden. Olofsson säger att V haft den attityden efter valet. – Nej Maud. Så är det inte. Alla ser att det ni vill, det finns inte längre. Och då måste man komma ut i verkligheten, svarar Andersson. Ida Gabrielsson, vice partiledare för Vänsterpartiet, tycker att Centerpartiets partiledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist nu bör få talmannens uppdrag att sondera. Gabrielsson delade uppmaningen på X i helgen – och upprepar nu budskapet i TV4:s ”Nyhetsmorgon”. V-toppen tycker att Centerpartiets röda linjer mot V och SD blockerar en ny regering. – De har satt ner fötterna lite i spagat och då går det inte att gå framåt. Utan man måste ändå samla en majoritet om man ska välja en statsminister. Och då har ju vi varit tydliga jättelänge att om vi ska vara med, då måste vi ingå i regering. Och det har de vetat. Jag tycker det är synd att de inte gjorde arbetet innan, att den här drömmen om mitten kanske inte gick i hamn – ”hur gör vi då?”, säger Gabrielsson i TV4 och fortsätter: – Därför tycker jag ju också att Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist kan få sonderingsuppdraget så att hon kan komma vidare när hon har kört den frågan i botten. På torsdag röstar riksdagen om S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson som statsminister, en omröstning som alla räknar med att hon faller i. Andersson själv uttryckte på tisdagen att hon tycker att statsminister Ulf Kristersson (M) istället ska få sonderingsuppdraget nu. Socialdemokraternas partiledare Magdalena Andersson anser att Vänsterpartiet behöver vidta ytterligare åtgärder för att kunna ingå i en regering. – Det finns åtgärder som Vänsterpartiet behöver göra om dom ska sitta i en regering. Och det är en av de saker som vi diskuterar med Vänsterpartiet, säger Magdalena Andersson i TV4 Nyhetsmorgon.

I P4 Nästa Stjärna tävlar han med Blow Your Brains Out (lyssna på hela låten i klippet) – en låt om hjärtekross efter ett tufft uppbrott. För att rösta på mlt. ; sms:a 2505 till 720 20 eller ring 0991-2505. Varje röst kostar 1 kr plus eventuell trafikavgift. Du kan rösta max tio gånger. Röstningen pågår fram till den 16 oktober då finalen i P4 Nästa Stjärna Stockholm avgörs i en direktsänd show på Musikplats Stockholm . Boka publikbiljett till finalen HÄR , det är gratis inträde och principen ”först till kvarn” som gäller. Grunden i vår journalistik är trovärdighet och opartiskhet.
